subject: Literature
title: The Catholic Index of Forbidden Books
description: A fast breakdown of The Catholic Index of Forbidden Books for builders.

hook.text: For over four hundred years, the Catholic Church maintained an official list of books that believers were forbidden to read.

buildup.text: The Index Librorum Prohibitorum was created in 1559 to combat the spread of Protestant and scientific ideas.

discovery.text: It banned Galileo, Descartes, Voltaire, Victor Hugo, and thousands of other authors across every discipline.

twist.text: The Index was only abolished in 1966, meaning the Church officially banned books well into the space age.

climax.text: Being on the Index often increased a book's sales, proving that censorship frequently promotes what it suppresses.

punchline.text: The banned books list was history's best reading recommendation.

quiz.question: When was the Catholic Index of Forbidden Books abolished?
options: In 1966, well into the space age
